steps.title: Begin with uniform stretch
steps.explanation: Mean stretch is 1 and the uneven-stretch amplitude is zero. Local compensation is then the identity everywhere.
steps.observe: Local J and both total volume ratios are 1 up to triangle-sum roundoff.

steps.title: Let local volume changes cancel
steps.explanation: The endpoint axial stretches are 0.6 and 1.4. Without transverse compensation, J equals the local axial stretch; the average remains 1.
steps.observe: Total continuum volume remains 1 while local J spans 0.6–1.4. A correct global volume cannot establish local incompressibility.

steps.title: Compensate every material section
steps.explanation: Set transverse stretch to 1/sqrt(lambda) at each section. This makes the exact map locally isochoric, but eight straight mesh cells only approximate its curved boundary.
steps.observe: Local J is 1 throughout. The measured mesh ratio is about 1.00248, an excess of 0.00247970 rather than an exact mesh-volume guarantee.

steps.title: Refine the geometric measurement
steps.explanation: Keep the same continuum map and increase only longitudinal cells from 8 to 128. This tests the straight-boundary approximation, not a different material.
steps.observe: Mesh-volume error falls to about 0.00000968811. The exact local and continuum volume ratios remain 1; the nonzero numerical discrepancy stays visible.

audit.finding: The old adapter showed only total volume and one fixed mesh, hiding the chapter’s key local-versus-global counterexample.
audit.change: Expose endpoint local J and mesh resolution with a cancellation, compensation and refinement experiment.
audit.remaining: A prescribed smooth map with straight-cell approximation; no force balance, material response or anatomical prediction. Lean matrix claims do not certify mesh code.
